channels.name: Tool pipeline
channels.evidence: Tool evidence rows: audit TOOL_CALL_ALLOWED, TOOL_CALL_DENIED or TOOL_CALL_FAILED, a metric row and a stdout descriptor, written by the composed recorder; for an authorized call each carries authorizationId and authorizationDigest, and one AUTHORIZATION_RECORD row holds the record; one EFFECTIVE_POLICY audit row and a signed .amc/effective-policy/<receiptId>.json per native session and guard set (compiled policy digest and revision, controls with enforcement and boundary, guard labels, guardrails, downgrades), cited in every authorization record's evidenceRefs
bypasses: A recorder that throws after the body ran is swallowed in ToolPipeline.execute; the effect stands and its row is missing
Exceptions and break-glass are not part of the authorization record (P2-24); tenant and deployment ids stay unregistered because the compiled plan does not carry them
A workspace with no active compiled plan runs without one; its receipts record the downgrade no_compiled_policy
Egress and deletion rules of a compiled plan are carried on the policy object and not enforced (P2-01); receipts label them enforcement none
The kernel tool service (src/kernel/services/toolServices.ts) enforces the compiled policy but writes no effective-policy receipt; it has no session writer

channels.name: Native shell
channels.evidence: NATIVE_SHELL_CONFINEMENT audit rows naming boundary (linux-bwrap or macos-seatbelt), network and processLimit; NATIVE_SHELL_EGRESS rows for every egress proxy decision; an unconfined-shell audit row before each opted-in unconfined command
bypasses: On macOS without a usable /usr/bin/sandbox-exec the shell is absent unless the operator passes the unsafe unconfined-shell opt-in; that shell runs with the user's full rights and is recorded, not confined

The macOS Seatbelt profile leaves reads outside its deny-list open; Mach lookups are limited to five system services (temp-directory helper, logging, notifications, user and group lookups), and POSIX shared memory and IOKit are not restricted
A signed shell egress allowlist is refused on Linux until the ADR-008 relay is reviewed and built
RLIMIT_NPROC counts all of the user's processes, so the cap is relative to the count at launch; there is no memory or CPU limit

channels.name: fs tools
bypasses: The shell and unconfined MCP servers reach the same files without these checks

channels.name: Network egress
channels.evidence: Gateway NETWORK_EGRESS_BLOCKED audit rows for proxy refusals (requesting agent, reason and resolved addresses), UNSAFE_PROVIDER_ROUTE audit rows for refused upstreams (reason, resolved addresses, upstreamId, agentId) and proxy rows recording the resolved addresses and the address a tunnel reached; NATIVE_SHELL_EGRESS rows for every shell proxy decision; NATIVE_WEB_EGRESS rows for every web_fetch and web_search egress decision; tool evidence rows for NETWORK_EXTERNAL tools
bypasses: networkEgressGuard applies only to tools declared NETWORK_EXTERNAL; MCP servers and extensions open sockets directly

Gateway upstreams pass by name, and their non-public addresses are allowed when gateway.yaml opts in (the baseUrl's literal host without an environment template, allowNonPublicAddresses on a validly signed file only, or loopback with allowLocalhost); the gateway still runs on an unsigned or invalid gateway.yaml (CONFIG_UNSIGNED), so the literal-host, allowLocalhost and proxy allowlistHosts IP-literal opt-ins are only as trustworthy as that file (P1-66)
A host allowlist cannot stop domain fronting through a listed host; the shell proxy pins the Host header for plain HTTP only
src/enforce/egressProxy.ts (checkEgressRequest) is not a proxy, is called only by tests/enforce-full.test.ts, allows every host when its list is empty and logs every decision as agentId system
There is no workspace-wide egress allowlist for in-process tools: web_fetch and web_search apply decideEgress to their own signed hosts, and the shell's allowlist governs only the shell (P2-13)

channels.name: Native web and session tools
channels.evidence: One NATIVE_WEB_FETCH, NATIVE_WEB_SEARCH, NATIVE_ASK_USER, NATIVE_TODO or NATIVE_PLAN call receipt (allow, deny or fail) per executed call, written before content is returned or a record is written; NATIVE_WEB_EGRESS rows before each web connection; tool evidence rows for every call, including guard denials
bypasses: No shipped policy lists the five tools, and no answerer or search provider is composed, so they stay denied until an operator signs a tools.yaml that lists them (profiles: P2-13)
Content from a granted origin is still attacker-controlled; it reaches the model fenced and labelled as untrusted data, which reduces but does not remove prompt injection

The todo and plan ledger check verifies the chain up to the newest row it finds; deleting the newest rows of an open session together with restoring an older record is caught only when the session writer next appends (STALE_HEAD)
An ask_user answer proves that a holder of the workspace auditor key answered, not which human; workspace keys give a local audit trail only

channels.name: MCP stdio
channels.evidence: Tool evidence rows for each call; mount refusals
bypasses: The server process is spawned unconfined with the user's rights: cwd is the workspace and env is the default environment plus the server's env; only the calls are governed

channels.name: MCP HTTP
channels.evidence: Tool evidence rows; mcp-catalog output and the mount receipt record the negotiated protocol and the OAuth issuer, scopes and expiry
bypasses: A broken 2026-07-28 tools/call stream leaves the remote outcome unknown; AMC reports TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and does not replay, so a side effect may have happened unrecorded
Protected-resource metadata may name any HTTPS authorization server; the operator approves it in the browser and grants are keyed by issuer, but AMC does not pin the issuer in config

channels.name: Provider calls
channels.evidence: Signed request/header and settlement rows; budget reservation rows
bypasses: No residency check on the route: bridgeResidencyHook (src/ops/productionWiring.ts) compares caller-supplied regions and nothing calls it

channels.name: Imports
channels.evidence: Import receipts; imported rows carry SELF_REPORTED unless a pinned third-party attestation binds them
bypasses: Imported content is untrusted text that later reaches model context; importers do not preserve original bytes

channels.name: Studio API and UI
bypasses: Claim kinds are not yet labelled on Studio and API output

channels.name: CLI
channels.evidence: Ledger rows for the commands that write them; no per-command record in general
bypasses: Authority is local file access plus the vault passphrase; the operator is trusted
amc init --skip-vault sets AMC_VAULT_PASSPHRASE to "skip-vault-" plus Date.now(), a guessable passphrase

channels.name: SDK and ACP
channels.evidence: The same session spine as the native runtime
bypasses: Execution is not yet one API across CLI, TypeScript, Python and Studio

channels.name: Extensions
bypasses: Executable extensions run only under Linux Bubblewrap; on other platforms they are refused, not confined

channels.name: Managed hooks
bypasses: Enforcement holds only while the external harness calls the hook; a harness run without it is not governed

channels.name: Notary
bypasses: Signing backends are a sealed key file or an operator-supplied external signer command; there is no native KMS, HSM or PKCS#11 provider

channels.name: Helm and Compose
bypasses: The Helm secret template ships change-me values for the vault, owner and notary secrets
Compose reads file secrets the operator must create; nothing checks them

failurePolicy.failure: Authority or mandatory evidence store unavailable before a protected effect
Evidence recorder fails after the effect happened
failurePolicy.behaviour: The effect stands; dependent actions wait; reconcile with the system of record

failurePolicy.failure: Process dies between dispatch and receipt
failurePolicy.behaviour: No automatic replay; reconcile by idempotency key

failurePolicy.failure: Approval stale, revoked, or bound to a different amount or recipient
failurePolicy.behaviour: Re-evaluate; the old approval cannot authorize the changed effect
Block the protected export; make no residency claim
Stop new effects; use a hazard-reviewed safe state where an abrupt stop is unsafe
Execution continues; mandatory evidence persists locally; dropped telemetry is reported
